issue.title: ACE TUI holds 2.3-2.5 GB RSS while idle on the Agents tab
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY: epic sase-v2 ("Fix ACE TUI freezes and prompt-input lag"), plan:202608/tui_freeze_regression.md. Its "Out of scope" section names this explicitly and directs filing it as a separate task bead: "The ~2.5 GB RSS observed in the reproducing process. It is suspicious and worth its own investigation, but nothing gathered here ties it causally to the freezes, and this plan should not grow to chase it. File it as a separate task bead." Routed here by the sase-v2 land agent on 2026-08-28.

OBSERVED: during the live forensics that produced epic sase-v2, one `sase ace` session on the reporter's 64-core host was measured at 2.3-2.5 GB RSS and 24 threads while sitting idle on the Agents tab (`ps`, same process the py-spy sample and the tui_stalls.jsonl window came from, 2026-08-28 08:38-08:45). That is one to two orders of magnitude above what a terminal UI process should hold.

NOT CAUSED BY sase-v2: the epic's six phases only removed work from hot paths (prompt-panel visual/anchor memoization, countdown activity gate, config-token refresh cadence, prompt-completion project-lookup caching, artifact-link target index). None of them allocates a new long-lived cache large enough to explain gigabytes, and the epic's own evidence explicitly declined to attribute the RSS to the freezes. Note that the epic's caches (per-generation/width section anchors, process-level project workflow-type/changespec-name caches, the per-load known-target index) are all small and bounded, but a footprint audit should still confirm that rather than assume it.

SCOPE: measure first, do not guess. Reproduce with a long-lived `sase ace` on a populated fleet, then attribute the heap before changing anything -- e.g. `tracemalloc` snapshots at intervals, `objgraph`/`gc` type histograms, or a memray run against the live TUI -- and check the obvious suspects the forensics already put in view: retained Textual `Strip`/`FIFOCache` render caches across many widths, the agent/artifact snapshot models kept per refresh, the artifact-link and link-index snapshot caches (`src/sase/ace/tui/relations/`), and anything keyed by a value that grows with session length rather than being replaced. Distinguish steady-state high-water from unbounded growth over time: a leak and a large-but-flat working set need different fixes.

VERIFICATION: a documented attribution of where the RSS goes, and either a bounded/reduced steady-state footprint on the same fixture with the number recorded, or a written finding that the footprint is expected with the evidence that says so.

task_type_fields.impact: Affects anyone who leaves the ACE TUI open, which is its normal usage. A multi-gigabyte resident set crowds out the rest of the host, and if any part of it is unbounded growth rather than a flat working set, a long-lived session degrades or is killed. Not currently known to cause the key-to-paint or stall regressions epic sase-v2 fixed.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/ace/tui/ (sase ace process; no single symbol attributed yet)
task_type_fields.repro: Start `sase ace` against a populated fleet, leave it on the Agents tab, and watch RSS: `ps -o pid,rss,nlwp,pcpu -p "$(pgrep -f 'sase ace' | head -1)"`. Reported measurement (2026-08-28, 64-core host, load ~8): 2.3-2.5 GB RSS, 24 threads, while idle on the Agents tab. Attribute the heap with tracemalloc/objgraph/memray against the same live process rather than from inspection.

payload.description: Proposed by this epic's plan ('Out of scope'). The epic's live forensics on one sase ace process is where the 2.3-2.5 GB measurement came from; read its py-spy and stall evidence first.
Adjacent footprint signal in the same ACE/Textual code: sase-j0 covers peak_worker_rss_kib and two ACE/Textual cost budgets. Different surface (test workers, not the live TUI), so not a duplicate.
